solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Happy with financial obligations? That’s debatable (11)

blocks.note: IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether being happy while in debt is possible, and a sceptic replies that the point is arguable.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark splits the clue in two: the first half is the wordplay, and 'That’s debatable' is the verdict, with 'debatable' as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A contentious claim is one people argue over, which is exactly what debatable means.

clue.text: School paintings etc intended to lose area in storage space (11)

indicators.note: MEANT has to lose the letter A, so it drops out

blocks.note: a comp is a comprehensive school, the standard British state secondary school
art covers paintings and the like
MEANT (intended) without A, the abbreviation for area

annotation.surface: A school's artwork was meant to be moved out of a storeroom to free up space.
annotation.walkthrough: COMP is British slang for a comprehensive, a state secondary school open to all pupils.
annotation.definitionFit: A compartment is a separate section of a container or cabinet where things are stored.

clue.text: Simba’s partner biting tail of jumpy antelope (5)

indicators.note: NALA takes Y between her teeth, so it ends up inside
a word's tail is its last letter

blocks.note: Nala is Simba's mate in The Lion King
last letter of jumpy, placed inside NALA

annotation.surface: A lioness from The Lion King snaps at the rear of a skittish antelope.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a hunting scene, and the prey in it turns out to be the answer itself.
annotation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope of southern Africa.

clue.text: Learned unlimited hors d’oeuvre introduced by European (7)

indicators.note: without its limits, the first and last letters, CRUDITES loses C and S
E comes first and ushers in the rest

blocks.note: CRUDITES, the raw vegetable starter, without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: An educated European tucks into an endless plate of starters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Learned' reads like a past-tense verb in the surface, but it is the adjective, pronounced as two syllables.
annotation.definitionFit: An erudite person has great learning, so 'learned' (scholarly) is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Upstanding character leaving island in plane? (4)

indicators.note: the letter I leaves the island's name, so it is removed

blocks.note: Tiree is an island in the Inner Hebrides, off the west coast of Scotland
the capital letter I is a single upright stroke, so it is the character that stands up; it is removed from TIREE

annotation.surface: An upright passenger gets off an island flight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plane' looks like an aircraft, and 'upstanding character' like a person of good morals; the plane is the tree, and the character is the letter I.
annotation.definitionFit: The plane is a common tree, lining many city streets, so 'plane?' defines TREE by example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Running watch confiscated by rising military leader from time to time (2,8)

indicators.note: the watch is taken into the officer's keeping, so CASIO goes inside
in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top, so NCO turns into OCN

blocks.note: a machine that is running is on
NCO = non-commissioned officer, turned up to OCN
Casio is a well-known make of digital watch, placed inside OCN

annotation.surface: A sergeant keeps confiscating a soldier's stopwatch now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Watch' is a brand name here, not a verb, and 'rising' turns only the officer, not the watch.
annotation.definitionFit: Something done on occasion happens now and then, which is from time to time.

clue.text: Only the principal’s involved in this pastime, supporting child’s play (6,8)

definitions.text: Only the principal’s involved in this

indicators.note: in a down clue, the supporting word sits underneath, so INTEREST comes after SIMPLE

blocks.note: an interest is a hobby or pastime

annotation.surface: A head teacher alone takes part in some easy game the children play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Principal' looks like a head teacher, but in finance the principal is the sum lent; simple interest is paid on that sum only, never on interest already earned.
annotation.definitionFit: Simple interest is calculated on the original principal alone, unlike compound interest, so only the principal is involved.

clue.text: Mythic hero quietly shivering, dangerously cold (11)

indicators.note: shaking the letters about scrambles their order

blocks.note: p = piano, quietly in music; joins the fodder

annotation.surface: A legendary hero stands quietly shivering, half frozen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shivering' fits the cold so snugly that it hardly looks like an instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Hypothermic describes a body whose temperature has fallen to a dangerous level.

clue.text: More enthusiastic French explorer abandoning cape after that chap (8)

indicators.note: CARTIER abandons C, so that letter drops out
after means following in order, so ARTIER follows HE

blocks.note: Jacques CARTIER, who explored the St Lawrence, without C for cape

annotation.surface: A keener French explorer leaves a headland behind, following some other man.
annotation.walkthrough: C for cape is a map abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Hearty means warm and enthusiastic, so heartier is more enthusiastic.

clue.text: Beat poet indicted for treason (5)

blocks.note: to beat is to strike again and again, as a drum or a heart does
the American modernist poet charged with treason for his wartime radio broadcasts from Fascist Italy

annotation.surface: A Beat poet stands accused of treason.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beat poet' reads as one phrase, like Ginsberg or Kerouac; the split falls between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Pound means to strike heavily and repeatedly, and Ezra Pound is the modernist poet.

clue.text: At home, kid’s rewritten opera (3,6)

indicators.note: the letters are written out again in a new order

annotation.surface: A child stays in and reworks an opera.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': kid is rewritten. 'At home' belongs to the fodder rather than giving IN.
annotation.definitionFit: The Mikado is Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera set in Japan.

clue.text: Show empty rocket ship abroad (6)

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: an expo is a trade show or exhibition

annotation.surface: An exhibition displays a hollow rocket before it is sent overseas.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ship' is a verb here, not the noun it seems beside 'rocket'.
annotation.definitionFit: To export goods is to send them abroad for sale.

clue.text: Evangelist cured me, snarled writer (6,2,9)

indicators.note: snarled means tangled, so the letters are knotted into a new order

annotation.surface: A preacher claims to have healed someone, who growls at the result.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Snarled' looks like a growl of anger but means tangled, as in snarled-up traffic.
annotation.definitionFit: Miguel de Cervantes wrote Don Quixote.

clue.text: Brevity of chapter about church head saving lives (11)

indicators.note: about gives ON, as in a book on or about a subject
CE keeps IS safe inside it

blocks.note: is = lives, exists; kept inside CE
a ness is a headland, as in Dungeness

annotation.surface: A short chapter tells of a church leader who saved lives.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like the leader of the church, but it is a headland; NESS appears in British place names such as Dungeness.
annotation.definitionFit: Conciseness is the quality of saying much in few words, which is brevity.

clue.text: Drama — this person backed country ahead of party, effacing when shunned by right (7,3,7)

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so USA becomes ASU
the country comes before the party
ERASURE is shunned by R, so that letter drops out

blocks.note: Reform UK is a British political party
ERASURE (effacing, the act of rubbing out) without R for right

annotation.surface: A patriot turns their back on their country for a party and quietly erases themselves from public life.
annotation.walkthrough: Reform UK is a right-leaning British party, which makes 'shunned by right' read as politics in the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is one of Shakespeare's problem plays, and drama is the broad class it belongs to.

clue.text: Secretary cut short group of druids? (5)

definitions.note: PAGAN is taken as the adjective here: belonging to druids and other followers of old religions

indicators.note: GANG is cut short, losing its last letter

annotation.surface: A secretary interrupts a gathering of druids.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Group of druids' looks like one phrase, but 'group' belongs to the wordplay and 'of druids?' is the definition; the question mark flags druids as one example of pagans.
annotation.definitionFit: Druids practised a pre-Christian religion, so their rites are pagan.

clue.text: Slowly notice a US soldier close to Oman’s capital (6)

indicators.note: a word's capital is its first letter, like a capital at the top of a column

blocks.note: an ad is a notice advertising something

annotation.surface: Someone gradually spots an American soldier stationed near Muscat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oman's capital' invites Muscat; it is only the O. 'Close to' just places it next to GI.
annotation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical direction to play slowly.

clue.text: Going in the wrong direction, detective and guards caught like statues (8)

indicators.note: the whole assembly runs backwards
PLUS stands guard round C

blocks.note: c = caught, in cricket scoring; placed inside PLUS

annotation.surface: A detective and his guards are caught heading the wrong way, frozen like statues.
annotation.walkthrough: DETPLUCS read backwards gives the answer. 'And' is a small word that does real work here.
annotation.definitionFit: Statues are sculpted, carved or modelled into shape.

clue.text: Middle Easterner is one tragic figure, on reflection (7)

indicators.note: seen in a mirror, I LEAR reads back to front

blocks.note: King Lear, Shakespeare's tragic king; I LEAR turned round gives RAELI

annotation.surface: Someone from the Middle East is a tragic figure when he thinks it over.
annotation.walkthrough: Only 'one tragic figure' is reversed; 'is' stays as it is at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym by nationality: Israel lies on the eastern Mediterranean, at the heart of the Middle East.

clue.text: Some applaud a numbing painkiller (8)

indicators.note: only some of the letters of 'applaud a numbing' are used

annotation.surface: Some people cheer a drug that dulls pain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Numbing' sits beside 'painkiller' as if describing it, yet it supplies the last three letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Laudanum, a tincture of opium, was the standard Victorian painkiller.

clue.text: Fights over tariffs? Head of finance quits afterwards in distress (5,4)

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
F quits AFTERWARDS, leaving it
distressed letters are knocked out of shape

annotation.surface: A finance minister resigns in distress after quarrels over import duties.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a political story, and the definition belongs to it.
annotation.definitionFit: Trade wars are conflicts in which countries raise tariffs against each other's goods.

clue.text: Letters from abroad? (8,9)

blocks.note: the surface reading is correspondence; the setter means people who let out property
the surface sends mail from overseas; the setter means renting out while living far away

annotation.surface: A question about post arriving from overseas.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Letters' looks like mail; it means people who let out property, and landlords who live away from it let from abroad.
annotation.definitionFit: An absentee landlord owns and lets property without living nearby, often in another country.

clue.text: Perhaps neon sign at vacant riverside works (5,3)

indicators.note: a vacant word has nothing inside, leaving its outer letters
the letters are worked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: RIVERSIDE emptied to its outer letters, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A neon sign hangs over an empty riverside factory.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Works' could be a factory in the surface; it is the instruction to rework the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Neon is one of the noble or inert gases, which barely react with anything; 'Perhaps' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Cheap conclusions of unpleasant, shallow death notice (3-3)

indicators.note: a word's conclusion is its last letter

blocks.note: last letters of unpleasant and shallow

annotation.surface: A shabby, shallow obituary ends on a nasty note.
annotation.walkthrough: TWO-BIT is American in origin: two bits were a quarter dollar, so a two-bit thing is worth very little.
annotation.definitionFit: Something two-bit is cheap and second-rate.

clue.text: At the outset, everyone disliked gross, embittered creep (4)

indicators.note: each word's outset is its first letter

blocks.note: first letters of the four words

annotation.surface: From the start, nobody liked the bitter, repulsive toady.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Creep' looks like a nasty person, the noun the surface wants; it is the verb, to move slowly.
annotation.definitionFit: To edge forward is to creep, moving gradually and carefully.

clue.text: Ignoring outsiders, pick secret name for summer bestseller? (3,5)

indicators.note: each word loses its first and last letters and keeps its middle

annotation.surface: A publisher keeps a summer blockbuster's author anonymous, ignoring outside opinion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bestseller' points to books, and 'secret name' to a pen name; the question mark admits it is a snack that sells best in summer.
annotation.definitionFit: Ice cream sells fastest in hot weather, so it is a summer bestseller.

clue.text: In recession, the US needs banks to follow (5)

indicators.note: the answer is found in the words that follow
going into recession means going backwards
the words either side bank the answer, holding it between them

blocks.note: hidden in tHE US NEeds, then read backwards

annotation.surface: An economist says that in a slump America needs its banks to lead the way.
annotation.walkthrough: The economic surface makes 'recession' look like a slump; it means going back, and the answer is read right to left.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what ensues comes after, usually as a consequence.

clue.text: Record broken by fashion company hosting Queen do (4,4)

indicators.note: EP is broken open and the rest is put inside
a host takes guests in, so CO takes R inside it

annotation.surface: A fashion label's party hosting the Queen breaks a record.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a party, which the surface builds; it is a hairdo.
annotation.definitionFit: The Eton crop was a short, slicked-down women's haircut of the 1920s, so it is a do.

clue.text: Loincloth from island hotel daughter also wears backwards (6)

indicators.note: I and HD wear TOO round it, so TOO goes inside
the finished string is read from right to left

blocks.note: H = hotel in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A hotelier's daughter from an island wears a loincloth back to front.
annotation.walkthrough: ITOOHD read backwards gives DHOOTI, a less common spelling of dhoti.
annotation.definitionFit: The dhooti, or dhoti, is a long loincloth worn by men in India.

clue.text: Perhaps Chopper Harris ultimately leaves my soccer lot injured (10)

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter
leaves means departs, so S goes away from MY SOCCER LOT
damaged letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: MY SOCCER LOT without S, then rearranged

annotation.surface: Chopper Harris, the famously hard-tackling Chelsea defender, walks off having hurt the speaker's team.
annotation.walkthrough: Ron 'Chopper' Harris was a Chelsea footballer; the definition takes only 'Chopper', a customised motorcycle with long front forks.
annotation.definitionFit: A chopper is a type of motorcycle, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Daft, daring act and innuendo regularly entertaining that woman’s supporter (14)

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals, every other one
FEAT and INED entertain HER BRA as guests between them

blocks.note: a feat is a bold achievement
a bra is a supporting garment

annotation.surface: A silly stunt and a string of double entendres are staged for the benefit of a woman's backer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' sounds like a fan or patron; it is an item of underwear.
annotation.definitionFit: Featherbrained means scatty and silly, as if one's head held only feathers.

clue.text: Dancing in leather before leaving (8)

indicators.note: before means ahead of, so TAN is placed ahead of GOING

blocks.note: to tan is to leather, beat; also tan is the colour of leather

annotation.surface: Someone dances in leathers before heading off.
annotation.walkthrough: Leather and tan are both slang for a thrashing: to leather someone is to tan their hide.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example made verbal: the tango is a ballroom dance, and the -ing form matches 'Dancing'.

clue.text: Gangsters cried about post celebrating a special occasion (9,5)

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a new order

annotation.surface: Mobsters weep over the mail sent for a birthday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' sounds like 'concerning' in the surface; it is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Greetings cards are sent in the post for birthdays, weddings and other occasions.

clue.text: Somewhere to sharpen extremely greasy TV judge’s parting (8)

indicators.note: take the extremes, the first and last letters
RINDER parts G from Y by standing between them

blocks.note: Judge Rinder, the British TV courtroom show fronted by barrister Robert Rinder; placed inside GY

annotation.surface: A slick television judge makes a farewell appearance.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': Rinder is parting GY. Judge Rinder is a daytime British TV courtroom show.
annotation.definitionFit: A grindery is a place where tools are ground sharp.

clue.text: Guide encountered soldiers around noon (6)

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so MET is wrapped round N

annotation.surface: A guide met a platoon at about midday.
annotation.walkthrough: OR for 'other ranks', soldiers below officer rank, is a crossword standard.
annotation.definitionFit: A mentor is an experienced adviser who guides someone.

clue.text: Pay too much on account of fight involving US agents (14)

indicators.note: COMPETE involves NSA, taking it inside

blocks.note: over = on account of, as in a row over money
to compete is to fight for something
NSA = National Security Agency; inside COMPETE

annotation.surface: Someone overpays because of a fight with American spooks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On account of' is a single idea, 'because of', as in a quarrel over money.
annotation.definitionFit: To overcompensate someone is to pay them more than they are owed.

clue.text: Film-maker and author are in France to adopt child (5,6)

indicators.note: ORWELL takes SON into his family, so SON goes inside

annotation.surface: A film-maker and a writer, both in France, plan to adopt a child.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Film-maker and author' reads as two people, but only the first is the definition; the author is Orwell.
annotation.definitionFit: Orson Welles directed Citizen Kane.

clue.text: Threat for mine workers sacked in the morning before pit’s opening (8)

indicators.note: a word's opening is its first letter

annotation.surface: Miners are laid off one morning before the colliery opens.
annotation.walkthrough: The mining surface makes 'sacked' and 'pit' look like part of the story; they are building blocks.
annotation.definitionFit: Firedamp is the methane that collects in coal mines and can explode.

clue.text: Chap overwhelmed by wine, Tango, water, and Frappuccino? (11)

indicators.note: in a down clue, MAN sits under PORT, weighed down by it

blocks.note: T = tango in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A man is swamped by a cocktail of wine, a fizzy drink, water and a sweet iced coffee.
annotation.walkthrough: Tango is also a British fizzy orange drink, so the surface reads as a list of drinks. Frappuccino blends frappé and cappuccino.
annotation.definitionFit: A portmanteau word fuses two words into one, as Frappuccino does with frappé and cappuccino.

clue.text: Survey caught touts periodically as a gamble’s admitted to (10)

indicators.note: take the letters at regular intervals
ON SPEC is let into C and TUS

blocks.note: done on spec = done as a speculation; goes inside

annotation.surface: A study finds ticket touts caught now and then as a bet is let in.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': 'as a gamble' is admitted.

clue.text: Outline house and title to be amended (10)

indicators.note: the letters are to be changed into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder; 'and' just joins the two

annotation.surface: A plan for a house and its deeds needs changing.
annotation.walkthrough: The property surface makes 'title' look like a deed; it is only letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A silhouette is the dark outline of a shape against light.

clue.text: Obscure items in lush heather covered with earth (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue, E sits on top as a cover

blocks.note: lush and sot are both slang for a drunkard
Erica is the botanical name for heather

annotation.surface: Strange objects are buried in thick heather under soil.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lush' looks like an adjective for heather; it is a noun, a drunk.
annotation.definitionFit: Esoterica are things known only to a few, obscure items or facts.

clue.text: Some time back (6)

blocks.note: to support a proposal formally at a meeting

annotation.walkthrough: 'Some time back' reads as 'a while ago'; split it into a unit of time and a verb meaning support.
annotation.definitionFit: Double definition: a unit of time sixty to the minute, and the verb for supporting a motion at a meeting.

clue.text: Distribute barely dry measuring device (5)

indicators.note: stripped bare, DRY loses its outer letters

blocks.note: to mete out is to distribute

annotation.surface: Someone hands out a gauge that shows things are only just dry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Barely dry' sounds like damp laundry; it strips DRY down to R.
annotation.definitionFit: A meter is a device for measuring, like a gas or water meter.

clue.text: Theatrical hypocrite cheers king very loudly during day (8)

indicators.note: FF comes during TUE, placed inside it

blocks.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
ff = fortissimo, very loud in music; inside TUE

clue.text: Russian leader turning to avoid Liberal in square (4)

indicators.note: LENIN turns round to NINEL
the result avoids L, dropping it

blocks.note: Lenin led the Bolshevik revolution; turned round to NINEL

annotation.surface: A Russian leader in a public square turns away to avoid a liberal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Square' looks like a town square, but it is a square number: nine is three times three.
annotation.definitionFit: Nine is a square number, three squared.

clue.text: Member making a bit of an entrance? (8)

definitions.text: Member making a bit of an entrance?

blocks.note: the surface reading is a club member; the setter means a structural member, an upright timber in a frame

blocks.clueFragment: making a bit of an entrance?
blocks.note: the surface means arriving with some fuss; the setter means forming part of a doorway

annotation.surface: A club member arrives with a small flourish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a club member and 'making an entrance' a grand arrival; in building, a member is a structural piece, and the jamb forms part of the doorway.
annotation.definitionFit: A door jamb is the upright side post of a door frame, literally a bit of an entrance.

clue.text: South American idiot on Guam initially enthralled by strange seaweed (9)

indicators.note: in an across clue, ASS goes on after G
initially means at the start, so only the first letter of Guam is used
RUM holds G and ASS captive inside it

blocks.note: ass = idiot; after G, inside RUM

annotation.surface: A South American fool on a Pacific island is captivated by some weird seaweed.

clue.text: Prevented Tesla blocking claim by journalist (7)

indicators.note: T blocks the way between AVER and ED, standing in the middle

blocks.note: T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

annotation.surface: A car maker stopped a reporter's story from running.
annotation.walkthrough: Tesla suggests the car company or the inventor; it is the physics unit, symbol T.

clue.text: Each one eats pastry (6)

indicators.note: ACE eats PIE, taking it inside

blocks.note: an ace is a one in cards and dice
a pie is a pastry; inside ACE

annotation.surface: Everybody has a pie.

clue.text: Obscure telecoms company captures short videos (7)

indicators.note: EE captures CLIPS, holding it inside

clue.text: Went back over president from the east meeting English Democrat (8)

clue.text: Artist beginning to draw two straight lines (5)

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: An artist starts sketching a pair of lines.

clue.text: Stun church official holding iron (6)

clue.text: This could be an op-ed with no conclusion? (10,7)

clue.text: Clergyman’s mutt sounded different (7,4)

indicators.note: the letters come out in a different order

annotation.surface: A vicar's mongrel barked in an odd way.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': Clergyman is 'mutt sounded' rearranged. 'Sounded' is only letters, not a hint that anything is heard.
annotation.definitionFit: Desmond Tutu was the Archbishop of Cape Town and an anti-apartheid campaigner.
